title: Ontario International Students Face 20% Fee Hike for Mandatory Health Insurance
excerpt: Annual UHIP premiums at 22 Ontario universities jump from $792 to $948 per student starting September 1, adding to the rising cost of studying in Canada.
body:
• The University Health Insurance Plan (UHIP) premium for individual international students at 22 Ontario universities rises from $792 to $948 annually — a 20% increase — effective September 1, 2026.
  • A family of three now pays $2,844 per year, up $468 from the current $2,376.
  • UHIP is compulsory for international students at member institutions, with few qualifying exemptions, and the cost is automatically charged alongside tuition.
  • The hike adds to a broader pattern of rising costs for international students in Canada, where study permit issuances have already dropped 50% for Indian nationals.

What Has Changed

Every international student enrolled at a major Ontario university will pay at least $156 more for compulsory health insurance when the new academic year begins on September 1, 2026. For individuals, the annual UHIP premium rises from $792 to $948. For a student with one dependent, the cost jumps from $1,584 to $1,896. For a family of three, the new rate is $2,844 — up from $2,376, according to CIC News, citing the updated UHIP rate schedule.

The increase applies across all 22 publicly funded Ontario universities that participate in the UHIP programme, from the University of Toronto and University of Waterloo to smaller institutions like Algoma University and Nipissing University.

Why Students Cannot Opt Out

UHIP is not optional. International students enrolled at member institutions are automatically charged the premium each term alongside tuition and other fees. Students can only opt out if they meet one of four narrow exemptions: coverage under the Ontario Health Insurance Plan (OHIP), coverage under another eligible pre-approved plan, diplomatic status, or coverage under a government-sponsored plan.

Few students qualify. Unlike provinces such as Alberta and British Columbia, which provide provincial health coverage to qualifying international students, Ontario does not extend OHIP eligibility to foreign nationals on student visas, CIC News reported.

Students must also enrol their dependents in UHIP if family members live with them in Ontario — a manual process that carries a $500 late-enrolment fee if not completed within 30 days of the dependent's arrival in Canada, according to the University of Ottawa.

What UHIP Covers — and What It Does Not

UHIP provides coverage up to $1 million CAD per policy year for medically necessary services, including primary care visits, diagnostic tests, emergency room treatment, and hospital surgeries. Coverage begins on the student's arrival date in Canada or the 10th of the month before the study period starts, whichever is later.

The plan is not equivalent to OHIP. It does not cover dental care, vision, prescription drugs, or many specialist services. Most international students purchase separate extended health insurance — typically through student society group plans — to fill these gaps. In many cases, that additional coverage is also mandatory.

The Cumulative Cost Burden

The UHIP increase does not exist in isolation. Indian students — the largest international student community in Canada — are navigating a rapidly escalating cost environment. Canada capped 2026 study permit issuances at 408,000, and the rejection rate for Indian student visa applications reached 80% in 2025, according to industry data. Proof-of-funds requirements have risen, and the Post-Graduation Work Permit now requires study in specific eligible fields.

"UHIP premiums may change each September 1 based on the cost of claims across all UHIP members and expected increases to health care costs overall."

— UHIP official rate page

For a student already paying $30,000-$50,000 in annual tuition, the $156 UHIP increase may seem minor in percentage terms. But layered onto visa fees, mandatory biometrics, living costs, and the extended health plan, each incremental increase narrows the financial margin that separates a viable study-abroad plan from an unsustainable one.

Looking Ahead

UHIP premiums are adjusted annually based on the cost of claims across all member institutions and projected healthcare cost increases. With Ontario healthcare costs continuing to climb and international student enrolment under pressure from federal policy changes, the trajectory suggests further increases in coming years. Students arriving for the September 2026 intake should factor the new rates into their financial planning from day one.
